proposals.before: For military merit he was made supervisor of the Feathered Forest, enfeoffed as Marquis of Weichang, and did not accept.
proposals.after: For military merit he was made supervisor of the Feathered Forest, enfeoffed as Baron of Weichang, and did not accept.
proposals.reason: Chinese 男 is the noble rank baron, not marquis (侯).

proposals.before: At that time the hegemonic design was newly begun and military and state affairs were broad; proclamations, orders, and edicts all issued from Yin and Cui Xian.
proposals.after: At that time the hegemonic design was newly begun and military and state affairs were broad; proclamations, orders, and edicts all issued from Yin and Cui Lingquan.
proposals.reason: Chinese 崔㥄悛 does not read as Cui Xian; 㥄 is Ling.

proposals.before: Sheep was Yin; 'horn' written was using a knife; 'Daoist' meant the deposed emperor's childhood name; the princess of Taiyuan had once been a nun, hence 'Auntie'; Yin's Zixian and Tianhe were both the emperor's brothers-in-law.
proposals.after: Sheep was Yin; 'horn' written was using a knife; 'Daoist' meant the deposed emperor's childhood name; the princess of Taiyuan had once been a nun, hence 'Auntie'; Zixian and Tianhe were both the emperor's sisters' husbands (姑夫).
proposals.reason: Chinese 子獻、天和 are not 'Yin's Zixian'; 姑夫 means the emperor's aunt's husband.

proposals.before: He also had a clerk call out men's names and by mistake called Lu Shishen Shichen; Shichen spoke up himself, and Yin said, "Master Lu, jade lustrous—therefore the jade radical. From nature it is so."
proposals.after: He also had a clerk call out men's names and by mistake took Lu Shishen for Shichen; Shichen spoke up himself, and Yin said, "Master Lu is jade-lustrous—therefore the jade radical."
proposals.reason: Chinese 誤以盧士深為士琛 means mistaking 士深 for 士琛; fused English and added clause obscure the Chinese.

proposals.before: Your servant and Zhan took the weight of state upon ourselves; Heba Ren and Hulu Jin cherished Gao Huan's foundation; we seized Zunyan and his fellows and brought them into the palace. We have not yet executed them; for our presumption we deserve ten thousand deaths."
proposals.after: Your servant and Zhan took the weight of state upon ourselves; Heba Ren and Hulu Jin cherished Emperor Xian's foundation; we seized Zunyan and his fellows and brought them into the palace. We have not yet executed them; for our presumption we deserve ten thousand deaths."
proposals.reason: Chinese has 獻皇帝 (Emperor Xian), not the personal name Gao Huan.

decisions.reason: s0023’s 賜爵魏昌男 uses the noble rank 男 (baron), not 侯 (marquis); Marquis of Weichang is a rank error and Baron of Weichang matches the Chinese.
s0054 names 崔㥄悛; 㥄 reads Ling and 悛 Quan, so Cui Lingquan is required and Cui Xian is an unsupported reading of the same characters.

decisions.after: Sheep was Yin; 'horn' written was using a knife; 'Daoist' meant the deposed emperor's childhood name; the princess of Taiyuan had once been a nun, hence 'Auntie'; Yin, Zixian, and Tianhe were all the emperor's aunts' husbands.
decisions.reason: 愔子獻、天和皆帝姑夫 lists Yin, Zixian, and Tianhe as all 姑夫; the before invents 'Yin's Zixian' and weakens 姑夫 to brothers-in-law, while the proposal drops 愔 and wrongly turns 姑夫 into the emperor's sisters' husbands.
誤以盧士深為士琛 is mistaking 士深 for 士琛, and Yin’s reply ends at 所以從玉; the before fuses the mix-up and invents 'From nature it is so,' which the proposed wording removes.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 誤以盧士深為士琛，士琛自言，愔曰：「盧郎玉潤，所以從玉。」

decisions.reason: s0151 has 惜獻皇帝基業; the title is 獻皇帝 (Emperor Xian), and substituting the personal name Gao Huan is not what the Chinese says.

claimRetractions.reason: Accepted r0002 shows Cui Xian exists only as a mistranslation of 崔㥄悛; the Chinese supports Cui Lingquan (c0091), not this English name.
